QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_19

question.text: Propensity Score Matching (PSM) is a quasi-experimental technique used when:

answer.text: The SIA wants to compute a confidence interval on a binary outcome
The SIA wants to monetise an environmental outcome for SROI
The SIA wants to run a focus-group discussion with beneficiaries
Randomisation is not possible and the SIA constructs a comparison group by matching treated units to untreated units on observable characteristics via a propensity score

explanation.text: The Logic: PSM matches each treated unit to one or more untreated units with similar observable characteristics (gender, age, income, education etc.), summarised as a propensity score (probability of being treated given those covariates). It approximates a randomised comparison using observational data. The Trap: Monetisation is a separate SROI step. Focus groups are qualitative. Confidence intervals are a statistical inference step, not a matching method. Cross-Exam Context: XV Research Analyst references matched-sample studies in event-study methodology. XXIII uses PSM as an SIA fallback when RCT is infeasible. Assessor's Pro-Tip: PSM is only as good as the covariate list — omitted-variable bias remains. Report the balance-check table (standardised mean difference <0.1 for each covariate post-matching) in your SIA working papers.
